slides.text: Four attempts (the third one will shock you!)
slides.original_description_html: Four attempts (the third one will shock you!)

slides.text: Attempt one: head-first into a wall • One prompt in Claude: “here are 52 questions, here’s a registry, go” • Context limits, rate limits, truncated output • LOL this did not work • Lots of tokens though!

slides.text: Attempt two: the version you’d draw on a whiteboard • Orchestrator + eight parallel researcher agents, one per section, shared state file • Hanging agents, silent blank results reported as success, state file corruption (it’s just vibes y’all) • Bonne nouvelle ! I hardened it for weeks and it got more robust!

slides.text: What even is truth? • Farquhar et al., Nature, 2024: confabulation • Kalai et al. (OpenAI), 2025: models are trained to guess, not to say “I don’t know” • Hicks, Humphries & Slater, 2024: it’s not lying; it’s indifferent to truth

slides.text: On the shoulders of giants • Huyen, 2022: ML systems fail silently; quality problems are harder to notice than operational ones • Husain & Shankar, 2025: start with error analysis, not infrastructure. Read 20 outputs before you build anything • Yan, 2025: “An LLM-as-Judge Won’t Save The Product”

slides.text: Attempt four: Stop—constraint time! • Lead with constraints, not requirements • The bar isn’t “fast”, it’s “faster than what exists now” • Reduce or remove the failure surfaces. Minimum viable product first, then evolve from there

slides.text: Simple, but not simplistic • Schluntz & Zhang (Anthropic), 2024: the best agent systems use simple, composable patterns, not frameworks • Willison, 2025: “an LLM agent runs tools in a loop to achieve a goal” (spoiler: that’s the whole abstraction)

slides.text: Seven things that work
slides.original_description_html: Seven things that work

slides.text: Guardrails; or “the art of scoping your sources” • Decide where the agent is allowed to look, before it’s allowed to think • Prioritise good sources and deny bad ones up front • Exhaust all good sources before hitting the information superhighway (it’s not actually that safe)
slides.original_description_html: 1. Guardrails; or “the art of scoping your sources” • Decide where the agent is allowed to look, before it’s allowed to think • Prioritise good sources and deny bad ones up front • Exhaust all good sources before hitting the information superhighway (it’s not actually that safe)

slides.text: Discipline; or “inference is not evidence” • Evidence includes a verbatim quote and a URL • Every question asked three different ways, even after a confirming hit • Gao et al., (HyDE), 2022: one phrasing is a sample, not a signal—sample more
slides.original_description_html: 1. Discipline; or “inference is not evidence” • Evidence includes a verbatim quote and a URL • Every question asked three different ways, even after a confirming hit • Gao et al., (HyDE), 2022: one phrasing is a sample, not a signal—sample more

slides.text: Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence Altman & Bland (BMJ), 1995
slides.original_description_html: Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence Altman & Bland (BMJ), 1995

slides.text: Logs; or “what the heck did the agent even do?” • Log the reasoning, not just the answer • This is how you build, debug, and improve • Can be operational, not just informational
slides.original_description_html: 1. Logs; or “what the heck did the agent even do?” • Log the reasoning, not just the answer • This is how you build, debug, and improve • Can be operational, not just informational

slides.text: Rigour; or “you can’t shortcut the methodology” • Once is not enough; use tokens intelligently • He et al. (Thinking Machines Lab), 2025: rerun variance is a property of the inference system • Variance is signal, be careful if there isn’t any
slides.original_description_html: 1. Rigour; or “you can’t shortcut the methodology” • Once is not enough; use tokens intelligently • He et al. (Thinking Machines Lab), 2025: rerun variance is a property of the inference system • Variance is signal, be careful if there isn’t any

slides.text: Prompting; or “operational != behavioural” • Operational: what to do, in what order, with what tool • Behavioural: how to reason, communicate, set boundaries • Shankar et al. (UIST), 2024: criteria drift; “you can’t write the rules before you’ve seen them fail”

slides.text: Human-in-the-loop; or “can’t do my job yet” • Involve a human when the variance is stable; domain expertise and intuition matter • Where the runtime file and LLM experimentation shine • Faster is only better if the results are good

slides.text: Sandboxes; or “basic agentic security hygiene” • Willison’s lethal trifecta: private data, untrusted content, external communication • Greshake et al., 2023: hostile pages can hide instructions aimed at the agent, not the human reading it • I use a kernel-level sandbox on a virtual machine, fwiw

slides.text: Everything, on one slide • Architecture can make you more robust without making you more correct • Different tasks need different model and harnesses • Guardrails, Discipline, Logs, Rigour, Prompting, HITL, and don’t forget Sandboxes
